The Manifest says:
TWO KINDS OF TECHNOLOGY
(208.) We distinguish between two kinds of technology, which we will call small-scale 
techn. and organization-dependent tech. Small-scale tech. is tech. that can be used by 
small communities without outside assistance. Organization-dependent tech. is tech that 
depends on large-scale social organization....
take the refrigerator for example. without factory-made parts or the facilities of a 
post-industrial machine shop it would be impossible for a handful of local craftsmen to 
build a refrigerator... it would be useless without a reliable source of electric power. 
So they would have to dam a stream and build a generator... and where would they get the 
gas for refrigeration? ... it is clear that if the ind. system were thoroughly broken 
dwn, refrigeration tech. would quickly be lost. The same is true of other organization 
dependent tech. Once it had been lost for a generation or so it would take centuries to 
rebuid it.... a long process of economic development and progress in social organization 
is required. And... there is no reason to believe that anyone would be interested in 
rebuilding industrial society. The enthusiasm for "progress" is a phenomenon peculiuar 
to the modern form of society, and it seems not to have existed prior to the 17th 
century...

Go back & read this section of the Manifesto.

> Not by reason as Ted first choice was by bombing people.

His first choice was outlined in his 1971 essay. Of course no one listened. Sadly, the 
only way to get attention for your cause usually is to do something outrageous or 
illegal.

> 
> Let see in order to force his changes down our throat you would need to
> burn all books dealing with technology

Yeah. I actually disagree with FC and agree with Meredith that burning books is wrong. 
You can pick your jaw up off the floor.

As far as "enforcing" lack of tech?? Let's see. Humans have mutually agreed that certain 
things are unethical even though they are possible. Such as slavery, cannibalism, etc. 
In general human societies refrain from these things.
Perhaps someday, after all the damages to the planet become apparent, humans will put 
rampant overdevelopment and tech. in the same category. The acceptable, "humane" way to 
live will be in small, semi-autonomous bioregions. But this may not happen until humans 
are FORCED out of their self-destructive ways, by an economic/ecological collapse or a 
large scale nuclear war that does what FC's pipe bombs failed to do: bring about the 
collapse of our present system.

--Shadow
